## Pull request overview

Fixes main-branch CI failures in the console app and plugin packages by addressing TypeScript type errors and a broken Vitest mock that unintentionally removed required exports.

**Changes:**
- Adjust Vitest mocking of `@object-ui/core` to preserve real exports while overriding `ExpressionEvaluator`.
- Update `AgGridImpl` context menu typings for ag-grid v35 (`DefaultMenuItem` union) and align return types.
- Remove/avoid unused imports/variables and relax `vi.importActual` typing where the module is only a transitive dependency.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListViewGroupingPropagation.test.tsx | Switches to `importOriginal` pattern so `normalizeQuickFilters` remains available while mocking `ExpressionEvaluator`. |
| packages/plugin-aggrid/src/AgGridImpl.tsx | Updates `getContextMenuItems` return typing for ag-grid v35 and adds a cast for default menu item strings. |
| apps/console/src/components/DesignDrawer.tsx | Removes unused `useState` import to fix TS6133. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/DesignDrawer.test.tsx | Uses untyped `vi.importActual` + cast for transitive Radix dependency; removes unused `container`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/DashboardViewSelection.test.tsx | Uses untyped `vi.importActual` + cast for transitive Radix dependency. |
</details>

The `item as DefaultMenuItem` cast bypasses the new AG Grid v35 typing and still allows arbitrary strings from `contextMenu.items` (your schema type currently permits `string`). This can hide invalid menu item keys at compile time and potentially surface as missing/ignored context menu entries at runtime. Consider tightening the `ContextMenuConfig.items` type to `DefaultMenuItem` plus any supported custom keys (e.g. your `export-excel` sentinel), and/or add a runtime guard that only forwards known default keys and converts unknown strings into a `MenuItemDef` (or drops them with a warning).
